Closes https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/31655 

1. Reproduced the freeze: Opened a project with a stalled session containing large diffs (multi-MB patches). Confirmed renderer freeze on fileDiffFromPatch → completePatchContents → parseDiffFromFile path.
2. Applied fixes and rebuilt: Ran electron-vite build in packages/desktop to produce a production build with all four fix layers.
3. Confirmed the fix: Reopened the same project. The session loaded without freeze. Large patches were:
Capped at 1MB during snapshot generation (snapshot/index.ts)
Discarded >1MB at the per-file diff endpoint (summary.ts)
Stripped >100KB from messages API responses (message-v2.ts)
Skipped content reconstruction on the frontend for patches >100KB, falling through to the fast parsePatchFiles path (session-diff.ts)
4. Verified diff display still works: Normal-sized diffs continued to render correctly with full before/after content reconstruction.
5. Checked no regression in snapshot generation: Ran existing snapshot tests via bun test in packages/opencode.

Following up on the SSE CLOSE_WAIT report from @AlexZander85 (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/20695#issuecomment-4232747716) with a code-verified mechanism and a fix: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/31922

Verified on current `dev` (mechanism + deterministic repro, no speculation):

- every `/event` and `/global/event` subscription buffers in an **unbounded** queue whose only cleanup signal is the response fiber ending — exactly the signal a CLOSE_WAIT peer never sends. The Effect migration preserved the pattern (`handlers/event.ts`: `Queue.unbounded` + `offerUnsafe` per connection).
- the instance endpoint filters by directory **after** buffering, so a stalled subscriber accumulates the full event firehose, not just its instance's events.
- repro: hold a connection without consuming the body and publish past capacity — the backlog grows with every event and the response stream never terminates. That exact scenario is now a regression test in `test/server/httpapi-event.test.ts`; it times out against the current handlers and passes with the fix.

The fix bounds the per-subscriber backlog (10k) and **ends the stream on overflow** rather than dropping events silently: what fit still flushes, finalizers unsubscribe the listener, and a live client reconnects and resyncs from the event log (safe because sync events carry a total order). A draining consumer is never cut — a companion test pushes 12k events through the 10k bound while staying connected.

This doesn't claim to be the whole megathread: the bmalloc/IOAccelerator native retention and `process.memoryUsage().rss` underreporting documented above are upstream Bun issues this PR doesn't touch. It removes one unbounded-growth mechanism with a deterministic repro.

Adding another reproduction from Windows + Paseo's OpenCode provider.

Environment:
- Windows 10/11 host
- Paseo 0.1.93 launching provider: opencode/cliproxyapi/gpt-5.5
- opencode CLI on PATH: 1.15.13 at C:\Users\Administrator\.bun\bin\opencode.exe
- Shared DB: C:\Users\Administrator\.local\share\opencode\opencode.db

Symptom:
Creating a new OpenCode-backed agent through Paseo fails immediately before model output. The first write path is session.next.agent.switched, then ppendMessage fails with:

`
SQLiteError: NOT NULL constraint failed: session_message.seq
    at appendMessage (...)
    at session.next.agent.switched (...)
    at SessionPrompt.createUserMessage (...)
    at SessionPrompt.prompt (...)
`

Local DB checks:
- PRAGMA integrity_check returned ok
- session_message schema included seq integer NOT NULL and unique index (session_id, seq)
- New failed sessions had zero message rows, so this was not caused by a corrupt existing row

This matches the version-skew explanation above: a newer migration had added the seq requirement, while the runtime writing the initial gent-switched message was still 1.15.13 and did not provide seq.

Temporary local workaround used only to unblock Paseo: backed up the DB, relaxed session_message.seq to nullable, and added an AFTER INSERT trigger to fill missing seq as MAX(seq)+1 per session. After that, a new Paseo OpenCode smoke-test agent completed and wrote:
- gent-switched, seq=0
- model-switched, seq=1

The better upstream fix still seems to be either runtime/schema compatibility detection or making the insert path handle missing/null seq for projected messages.
